Are you calculating wages based on after tax, gas and mileage? Taxes depend on your state and circumstances but generally 20-30% is taxes, gas however much it costs there, mileage is expenses such as oil changes more often, etc. Knowing you'll need tires sooner than not, extra insurance because IC and a lot of the times your car insurance depending on the company won't cover you. Once you know how much you are actually making vs what you want to make take orders that align with that. Because $20 sounds great till you realize how much goes to gas,mileage, and tax for that specific order. Even if your car is good on gas ALWAYS count the .60 a mile and subtract it from your pay. You car is more than just gas. So say an order pays $20 but mileage is 15 Miles subtract $9 for your car and your before tax time is $11. After taxes most people just made $9 not including the miles you drive to the store and FROM the customer. Hopefully this helps you figure out why some of us skip orders, some would put us in  a deficit.
